If I could change one thing about iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, I would eliminate the new top-to-bottom swipe gesture for invoking Siri AI. There are already enough ways to invoke Siri, and I've always been accustomed to swiping from the top down to open Notification Center on my iPhone and iPad, so this new gesture actually has little impact on my usage habits.

Moving on to the Mac, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost entirely good news. Even though it's already the end of August, the new beta versions are still incorporating many delightful changes. However, before macOS 27 officially launches next month, there's still one more change I'd like to see.

macOS 27 Golden Gate makes it harder to see the battery percentage on MacBook

macOS 27 Golden Gate has redesigned the battery control in the menu bar. By default, it only shows the battery icon, not the percentage.

At first glance, this doesn't seem like a problem, and I've personally turned off the percentage display on my iPhone—the iPhone uses a similar battery icon as well. However, I've always liked being able to see the battery percentage on my Mac.

If you enable the 'Show Percentage' option in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the number is placed inside the battery icon. I assume Apple wanted to maintain design consistency with the iPhone running iOS 27.

Placing the percentage inside the iPhone battery icon was a compromise Apple made to accommodate the limited space to the right of the 'M-shaped notch' or Dynamic Island. But on the Mac, even in the menu bar, I've never experienced a shortage of screen space.

Since the first developer beta, I've been running macOS 27 Golden Gate on a 15-inch MacBook Air. I've found that because it's not easy enough to read, I generally check the battery percentage less often.

I hope Apple reconsiders this point in future design decisions, especially as more users find this design problematic. Until then, I've at least found a workaround myself.

I used Codex to write a simple menu bar utility that clearly displays the battery status and percentage to suit my own needs. If you find it useful, you can download and install it for free here.
